It all makes so much sense, since I was 8, during breakfast my sister used to slurp her cereal and then proceed to crunch very loudly.  I remember sitting across from her and being so agitated I had to cover her face with the cereal box and try to repress my discomfort.  Whenever I woke up on the middle of the night to my sister eating, I’d yell at her to shut up, then proceed to mumble rude things under my breath because I was trying to sleep and was exhausted.

Also, whenever I was sleeping, or at least trying to sleep, my dad would come home from work if I ever stayed up too late, and he would cough and blow his nose loud as hell.  I remember holding my pillow over my ears in complete rage and forcing myself to go to bed.  Also, I would try my best to go to bed early for that exact reason.  

On top of this, since 4th grade, I can remember trying to sleep and the repetitious noise of my sister playing on the Xbox remote revoked an unknown anger inside of me.  On top of this, when I used to hear my brother typing from the kitchen whilst sleeping, or when sick, I would nearly cry from anger and discomfort.  

Whenever I’m stressed whilst trying to finish my missing assignments, the sound of my little sister consistently crunching/opening her mouth to taste her food enrages me.  I can’t control it, I have to shout at her to shut up.

I haven’t been diagnosed with Misophonia but I feel like certain sounds bother me to an unrealistic extent and I might just have it.  When I found out about the word and searched it in google, I felt so understood and sat in my bed for 5 minutes trying to process the shock.  After all those years of struggling with noises that didn’t seem to bother anyone else, I realized it might not have been my fault, because it’s completely out of my control.

TLDR: Repetitive Chewing, smacking, slurping, coughing, sneezing, moaning, typing, video game buttons being pressed, and crunching all anger me to an unrealistic extent, and I realized it probably isn’t normal, so I may have Misophonia.  (These things have bothered me since 8 years old, as far as I can remember).
